newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel eases foreign limits on Bezeq.
newsitem.headline: Israel eases foreign limits on Bezeq.

text.p: Israel's cabinet voted on Friday to ease restrictions on foreign shareholdings in Bezeq Israel Telecom Bezeq and declare certain of the company's services as "critical" to ensure their future survival.
"Now we are no longer discriminating between foreign and local companies," Communications Minister Limor Livnat told Reuters.
While the decision would enable Cable & Wireless Plc. to increase its shareholding in Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications carrier, Livnat said it was not directly related to the British company.

Cable & Wireless acquired 10 percent of Bezeq in the Israeli share market nearly two years ago without informing the Israeli government of its intentions and has indicated it would like to become a strategic shareholder by raising its stake further.
The two sides have been locked in negotiations on the matter since then.
Under the cabinet decision, holdings by foreign companies like Cable & Wireless will no longer be restricted to a 10 percent ceiling without authorisation of the communications minister.

Like domestic investors they will only need to get approval as they reach threshholds starting at five percent and working their way up to 25 percent, which is about equal to Bezeq's total public float.

Livnat said she had informed Cable & Wireless officials about the cabinet decision but said it was "completely unrelated" to the negotiations. She termed the talks at a "very advanced stage" and said she expected them to be completed within the next few weeks.
Clarifying Cable & Wireless's future status at Bezeq is regarded as a key condition for the company to go ahead with a planned global offering later this year.
Livnat said the decision to declare some Bezeq services as critical was to ensure such services were provided even if the government is reduced to a minority shareholder by privatisation.
"We declared certain Bezeq services critical as a substitute for golden shares," she said.
